A.name: Mayor Jared Gray
A.basis: opens the 4:00 work session ('Welcome to the City Council meeting... June 2nd at 4 PM'), excuses the two remote members, runs every agenda item, and calls the roll on the closed-session motion; addressed as 'Mayor'

C.name: Kimberly Ruesch (Administrative Services Director)
C.basis: presents the credit card policy and the T-Mobile contract answers; Councilmember Wright says 'With that explanation, Kimberly, then I don't have any issues,' and the mayor asks 'Kimberly' to open the policy session with a prayer

D.name: Lacie Messerly (City Recorder)
D.basis: gets the remote members unmuted at the start ('Brett, can you hear us okay?'), and after the mayor says comment cards go 'to our city recorder Lacey... and we'll go to Lacey,' she reads each public commenter's name off the cards (Holly Thomas, Cole Thomas, Tracy Knight, Jeff Bean)

E.name: Councilmember Brett Wright
E.basis: answers 'Yes, I can. Thank you' when asked 'Brett, can you hear us okay?', and replies to the mayor's 'Councilmember Wright, I know you had a lot of questions on this one' with the gift-card/treasurer questions; participates remotely from the water conference

F.name: City IT staff (unnamed)
F.basis: HR defers the technical questions to him ('I'll let him speak to that'), and he answers on contract-renewal cycles, three competing quotes, how the carrier bundles free devices into the line charge, and BYOD device 'profiling' — he is never named on the recording; the mayor separately says the city 'asked Carson to look into adding Verizon towers,' which may or may not be this person

G.name: Angela Valenzuela (Human Resources Manager)
G.basis: presents the employee-manual cell phone change the mayor introduces as 'Angela Valenzuela from our Human Resources,' and is asked mid-discussion 'Angela, read that part again that you just read'

H.name: Laura Gallardo (Teen CERT graduate)
H.basis: introduced by the public safety director as the graduate who will address the council, then opens 'my name is Laura Gallardo, and I had the opportunity to do this internship this past semester'

I.name: Councilmember Rich Wood
I.basis: argues 'being a religious organization owning property shouldn't give you specific development rights'; Whiting says 'I agree with Councilmember Wright, or Wood here' right after him, Clark cites 'what Councilmember Wood's saying,' and Huish falls 'on the side of Craig and Rich here'

J.name: David Salazar (Assistant City Engineer)
J.basis: answers 'I've got 5 quick slides' when the mayor introduces item 14A as 'that's David Salazar,' then presents moving night-work approval to the city engineer ('your neighbor Joe can't go dig up his driveway in the middle of the night')

K.name: Councilmember Craig Whiting
K.basis: answers 'Yes' when the mayor calls 'Councilmember Whiting?' in the closed-session roll call; Clark also asks him directly, 'Councilmember Whiting, do you want something to be added in here that it needs to be reviewed like every 12 to 18 months?'

L.name: Councilmember Melissa Clark
L.basis: answers 'Yes' when 'Councilmember Clark?' is called in the closed-session roll call and is recorded as the second on that motion; Wood twice defers to 'Melissa's point' immediately after she speaks

N.name: Councilmember Zac Huish
N.basis: answers 'Yes' when the mayor checks in with 'Council Member Hewers' (the recording's spelling of Huish) before the closed-session vote, proposes the '$60 a month reimbursement' his own company uses, and discloses to bond counsel 'I won't be voting on this issue, so I'm just asking'; joins remotely from the water conference

O.name: Dave Ulibarri (Public Safety Director)
O.basis: introduces himself as 'Dave Ulibarri, Public Safety Director and slash Emergency [Manager]' and presents the 17 Teen CERT internship graduates, reading out each student's name

P.name: Rob Hobbs (Senior Planner)
P.basis: delivers the Scenic Mountain 223-property rezone presentation after the mayor says 'Mr. Hobbs is going to tell us more about it,' explains starting 'on the periphery, like you might start on a puzzle,' and agrees to research UDOT frontage duties

Q.name: Marcus Draper (City Attorney)
Q.basis: answers Wood's 'Mark, I don't know if you're the person to ask this question' about bonding private improvements ('they can't force someone to bond for private improvements under current state law') and presents the Forged Fiber 37 / AT&T franchise agreement the mayor hands off with 'I know Marcus has this one'

R.name: Gwen Whiting (Cedar Valley internship teacher)
R.basis: states 'my name is Gwen Whiting. I'm the internship teacher at Cedar Valley, and Dave and I started this program 4 years ago,' then reads the former student's scholarship letter

S.name: Ben (City Manager)
S.basis: gives the city manager information items and the upcoming-events report; Councilmember Wright prompts 'Ben, you're waiting to do this in the policy session,' and he reads the retirement statement 'on behalf of the mayor and council, city staff, and the residents of Eagle Mountain'

T.name: Tracy Knight (resident)
T.basis: speaks immediately after the recorder calls 'Tracy Knight' from the comment cards; a retiree from Southern California who asks who was notified of the Horizon project and whether slope and street-width variances have been granted

U.name: Brandon Larsen (Community Development Director)
U.basis: the city manager turns the church rec-building item 'over to Brandon,' and he hands it on to the planner; later presents the BCS third-party plan review contract the mayor introduces as 'This is Brandon Larson'

V.name: Steven Lehmitz (Planner)
V.basis: presents the three code conflicts on the church recreation building (parking-lot walkway, 40-foot height, blank east wall) after Brandon says 'I'm going to turn the time over to Steven Layman'; the mayor closes the item with 'So, Steven, I'm going to come to you'

W.name: Holly Thomas (resident)
W.basis: speaks when the recorder calls 'Holly Thomas'; says it is the second time the Horizon item has been pulled, that she owns 10 acres abutting the ridgeline, and that she has dismantled countless campfire rings on the hillside

X.name: Faina Kofod (retiring city leader)
X.basis: invited to speak by the mayor ('Finn, I might put you on the spot') after the city manager's retirement tribute, which lists her service as city recorder, administrative services director and 'most recently, assistant' — the audio clips the last title; she says she has watched the city 'go from really nothing' to almost 80,000 people. The recording renders her name as Faina Kofod, Fina Kofod and Finn Coffett, so the spelling is uncertain

Y.name: Brad Patterson (bond counsel, Gilmore & Bell)
Y.basis: joins by phone as the bond counsel Kimberly says is 'on the line'; tells Huish the call features are set 'when the bonds are actually sold into the market' and signs off so the council can carry on 'without having to be bored by bond nerd stuff'

Z.name: Holly Reimer (resident)
Z.basis: speaks when the recorder calls 'Holly Reimer'; asks the council to extend Silver Lake Parkway to the new high school, citing the single way in and out and the missing sidewalk on the south side of Pony Express Parkway

AA.name: Steve (staff liaison to the Community Services Board)
AA.basis: presents the $25,369 county recreation grant and the board's asphalt-trail recommendations from online, and speaks for the board again on its rules and regulations ('This is another one we do have Steve online'); addressed throughout as 'Steve', but his department is never stated on the recording

AB.name: Jeff Bean (resident)
AB.basis: the last speaker the recorder calls before the recording cuts off; echoes the Silver Lake Parkway extension request and says the neighborhood is 'still waiting for a traffic study'
